How it's made

Where the red comes from.

Waakye (say "waa-chay") started in northern Ghana. The colour has nothing to do with tomato. It comes from dried sorghum leaf stalks cooked right in the pot.

  1. 1

    Soak

    Black-eyed beans rest in water overnight so they cook through soft and even.

  2. 2

    Stain

    The beans boil with a bundle of sorghum leaves. The water turns a deep wine red.

  3. 3

    Steam

    Rice goes into that red water and steams slowly until every grain drinks it in.

  4. 4

    Pile

    Onto the leaf it goes, with talia, gari, egg, wele, plantain and a dark crown of shito.

    Our story

    A taste of home, in Houston.

    Every Ghanaian knows the waakye queue. The early-morning line, the woman with the big pot, the leaf-wrapped parcel you carry to work. Mai Waakye brings that plate to Texas, cooked the way it's done at home.

    No shortcuts on the things that matter: sorghum leaves in the pot, shito made in-house, and plates built to order so nobody gets a side they didn't ask for.

    Say it like home:"waa-chay"
